Without a computer: Shizuku

Shizuku runs commands with the rights adb has, started by Android\'s %1$s instead of a computer. Do “Let Robot repair that itself” first: once Robot may write that one setting, it sets its speech recognizer again by itself after every restart, so you need Shizuku only once.
1. Install Shizuku

By RikkaApps, only from its own releases (github.com/RikkaApps/Shizuku/releases) or from IzzyOnDroid. To check it\'s genuine: its package is moe.shizuku.privileged.api, and its signing certificate, which an app verifier such as AppVerifier shows, is the one the Shizuku project publishes. Android then refuses any update signed with another key.
2. Start it with %1$s
%1$s: tap %2$s seven times. Then %3$s › %4$s (it needs Wi-Fi). In Shizuku, start it through %4$s and pair it as Shizuku shows. After every restart of the phone, start Shizuku again this way.
3. Give rish to Termux
In Shizuku: Use Shizuku in terminal apps › Export files, and pick Termux\'s home folder (Termux, in the file picker\'s menu). Then paste this line in Termux:
Copy the line to paste in Termux
4. Allow Termux, and only Termux
In Termux, run %1$s once: Shizuku asks whether Termux may use it. Allow it. It answers uid=2000(shell).
5. Run each fix
Each fix\'s page has its command for rish: the same command without “adb shell”, as rish -c \'…\', with Copy. With Termux set up in Robot, Robot can send it to Termux for you.
Shizuku gives adb\'s power to every app you authorize in it: authorize only Termux, and stop Shizuku when you\'re done (Shizuku\'s Stop, or turn %1$s off).
